question: What have recent works on reinforcement learning for reasoning in LLMs (since DeepSeek-R1) established about reward design, policy optimisation, sampling, open problems, resources and applications, and how can RL be scaled further toward ASI?
contributions: Preliminary definitions of RL modelling for LRMs and an outline of frontier reasoning models since OpenAI o1 (Sec 2.1, 2.2).
A review of foundational components: reward design, policy optimisation and sampling strategies (Sec 3).
A discussion of foundational and controversial problems: RL's role, RL vs SFT, model priors, training recipes, reward type (Sec 4).
A survey of training resources: static corpora, dynamic environments, RL infrastructure (Sec 5).
A review of applications (coding, agentic, multimodal, multi-agent, robotics, medical) (Sec 6) and future directions (Sec 7).

limits: A survey: it runs no experiments, and nearly every figure it relays is quoted without model, benchmark, seed or baseline, so it works as a map to the cited papers.
The authors concede the field has inconsistent experimental settings, incomplete reporting and conflicting conclusions (Sec 4.4).
The authors note there is still no standardised, reproducible OOD benchmark to separate generalisation from memorisation (Sec 4.2).
The 'sharpening vs discovery' dichotomy is left unresolved; the authors suggest asking under which conditions each dominates (Sec 4.1).
Coverage ends around September 2025 (arXiv v3 dated 2025-10-09); the field has moved on since.
Section 6.5 states that robotics RL outside the VLA setting is out of scope; RL for diffusion image models is deferred to other surveys.
practices: Use rule-based verifiable rewards (accuracy plus format) wherever a reliable verifier exists, since learned reward models suffer reward hacking at scale (Sec 3.1.1).
Combine verifier and reward-model scores with a constant coefficient so correct responses can be ranked, avoiding all-0 or all-1 reward groups (Sec 3.1.5).
Use group baselines (GRPO, RLOO) and Pass@K-aligned objectives to stabilise training and widen exploration (Sec 3.1.5).
Prefer critic-free algorithms with sequence-level rewards in rule-based environments to avoid critic-induced reward hacking and cut compute (Sec 3.2.3).
Use Clip-Higher (eps_high above eps_low) and dynamic sampling that drops all-correct and all-wrong prompts, as in DAPO (Sec 3.3.1, 4.4).
Reconsider KL regularisation for reasoning RL; many recent recipes drop it to simplify and save memory (Sec 3.2.5).
Watch for entropy collapse; control it via temperature, clip-higher, or Clip-Cov/KL-Cov (Sec 3.2.5, 3.3.2).
Stage the context length, starting short (e.g. 8k) and growing to 16k, 24k or 32k; filter overlong samples at short budgets and penalise them at long budgets (Sec 3.3.2).
Start RL from a base model rather than an instruct model; for weak-prior families such as Llama, strengthen priors with mid-training before RLVR (Sec 4.3).
Validate RL claims across model families with different priors, since Qwen gains under spurious rewards that Llama and OLMo do not (Sec 4.3).
Use hybrid or alternating SFT+RL (UFT, SRFT, LUFFY and others) rather than treating SFT and RL as exclusive (Sec 4.2).
Report unified protocols and explicit scalability-performance-cost curves so a method is shown to hold at scale (Sec 4.4).

terms.definition: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards: a programmatic verifier (answer checker or unit tests) replaces a learned reward model, giving binary checkable signals.
The ease of training AI systems to perform a task is proportional to the degree to which the task is verifiable.
Accuracy rewards compare a delimited final answer (e.g. \boxed{}) with ground truth or run unit tests; format rewards require reasoning inside <think></think> and the answer in a separate field.
A reward model that produces structured critiques, rationales and preferences rather than a scalar score.
Sharpening: RL only reweights correct responses already in the base model. Discovery: RL finds patterns the base would not produce by repeated sampling.
Decoupled PPO clipping with an upper bound set higher than the lower one so unlikely but useful tokens can rise more freely.
R1-Zero applies large-scale rule-based RL directly to a base model; R1 adds a brief cold-start SFT stage before RL.
A late pre-training phase in which the learning rate decays while the data mixture is reweighted toward small high-quality sources such as code, maths and curated QA.
The cumulative reward of the whole trajectory for prompt x, typically with gamma=1 for finite horizons; reduces to R(x,y) with a sequence-level reward.
